blog.title: Reading only gets you so far.
blog.body: Every article here ends the same way: come and try frames on. Twenty minutes in the shop beats an afternoon of research.

hero.title: Find the frame that feels like you.
hero.body: Fashion eyewear and prescription glasses, carefully selected for everyday life and personal style.

storyPoints.label: How we work
storyPoints.value: Fitted in person, adjusted for life

discover.title: Two ways to see, one way to choose.
discover.intro: Whether you are here for a prescription or purely for the look, the process is the same: try on more than you expect to, and keep the one that still feels right after five minutes.

philosophy.title: More than a pair of glasses.
body: Choosing glasses is not only about seeing clearly. It is about finding a frame that fits your face, your lifestyle, and the way you want to express yourself.
So we take our time. We look at proportion before we look at price, we say when something is not working, and we fit every frame properly before it leaves the shop.

family.title: A family business, built around people.
body: For years, we have believed that choosing glasses should feel personal — an unhurried conversation, not a transaction across a counter.

KOJIKANE EYEWEAR is run by one family in Nonthaburi. The people who help you choose a frame are the people who own the shop, which means the advice you get is the advice we would give someone we expect to see again.
Many of our customers first came in for a repair, or because a neighbour sent them. That is still how most people find us.
family.pullQuote: We would rather you came back than bought quickly.

featured.title: A selection, not a catalogue.
featured.intro: Six frames we are recommending at the moment, across fashion, prescription, classic, minimal and statement shapes. Everything here is in the shop — come and put them on.
featured.note: We do not sell online. Frames are photographed for reference only — fit, weight and colour are best judged in person, which is why every pair we sell is fitted at the shop.

services.title: What we do at the counter.
services.intro: Everything that happens after you choose a frame — measuring, fitting, lenses, and the small adjustments that keep a pair comfortable for years.
services.caption: Every frame is adjusted before it leaves the shop — and re-adjusted whenever it needs it.

journal.title: THE KOJIKANE JOURNAL
journal.subtitle: Stories, guides, and ideas about eyewear, style, and everyday vision.

fashion.title: Fashion Eyewear
fashion.description: Shapes with a point of view — sculptural acetate, coloured translucents, and silhouettes that change the balance of a face. Worn with or without correction.

prescription.title: Prescription Eyewear
prescription.tagline: Clear vision, comfortable fit, everyday confidence.
prescription.description: Frames selected for how they sit, how light they feel after eight hours, and how well they carry your lenses. Fitted and adjusted in person.

aoi.note: A rounded silhouette in translucent honey. Softens a strong jaw and reads warm against most skin tones.

nagi.note: Barely there at the temples, under 12 grams on the nose. The frame people forget they are wearing.

kumo.note: Oversized and square, with a flat top line. Best on faces that can carry width — try it before you decide.

sumi.note: A keyhole bridge and gentle panto shape. The frame we recommend most often, and the one people keep longest.

hikari.note: Nothing between you and the room. Suits mid-index single-vision lenses and quiet, professional dress.

mine.note: An angular cat-eye with a lifted outer corner. Small on paper, decisive in person.

index.title: Frames worth making a journey for.
index.intro: We keep a tight selection rather than a wall of stock — shapes we would happily wear ourselves, in materials that last. Everything shown here is in the shop.
index.featuredIntro: A cross-section of the shop, from the quietest titanium to the most decisive acetate. No prices online — we would rather talk you through the options in person.

fashionPage.howTitle: Style is a decision, not a size.
fashionPage.body1: A fashion frame does something a prescription frame does not have to: it changes the impression you make before you have said anything. That is worth taking seriously, and it is worth trying on more than you planned to.
fashionPage.body2Start: Fashion eyewear here does not mean glasses without lenses. Almost everything on these shelves can carry a prescription — the difference is where we start from.

edits.title: Shape before colour
edits.text: Start with the outline. A frame that flatters in clear acetate will flatter in tortoiseshell — the reverse is rarely true.

edits.title: Proportion, not size
edits.text: A frame should be about as wide as the widest part of your face. Everything after that is preference, not rule.

edits.title: One decisive detail
edits.text: A lifted corner, a coloured temple, a heavier top line. One is style. Three is costume.

fashionPage.inStoreTitle: Frames with a point of view.
fashionPage.inStoreIntro: Shapes that change the balance of a face. Try the one you would not normally reach for — it is usually the one people remember.

prescriptionPage.body1: A prescription pair has to do two jobs at once — sit well on your face and carry your lenses without distortion. Frame depth, bridge width and lens index all change the result, so we measure before we recommend.
prescriptionPage.body2Start: Bring your most recent prescription from your eye examination. If you are choosing between a quiet frame and something with more character, you can have both —
prescriptionPage.body2Link: most fashion frames take prescription lenses

notes.title: Bring your prescription
notes.text: A current prescription from your eye examination lets us match frame depth and lens type properly on the first visit.

notes.title: Weight is comfort
notes.text: How a frame feels in the first minute and after eight hours are two different things. We fit for the second one.

notes.title: Adjustment is included
notes.text: Frames move with wear. Bring them back whenever they slip — adjustment is part of buying from us, not an extra.

prescriptionPage.inStoreIntro: Titanium, rimless and classic acetate — the frames that suit long days and stronger prescriptions.

page.title: The part that happens at the counter.
page.intro: Choosing a frame takes twenty minutes. Making it fit, choosing the right lenses and keeping it comfortable for years is the rest of the job — and it is the part we care most about.
page.honestTitle: We will tell you what you do not need.
honestBody: Lens coatings, indexes and add-ons are where most opticians make their margin. We would rather explain the difference honestly and let you decide — including when the cheaper option is the better one for your prescription.
The same goes for frames. If something does not suit you, we will say so, even if it is the most expensive pair on the shelf.

prescription-eyewear.title: Prescription Eyewear
prescription-eyewear.summary: Frames matched to your prescription, assembled and checked in store.
prescription-eyewear.detail: Bring your current prescription and we will help you choose a frame that suits both your face and your lenses — frame depth, bridge width and lens type all affect how the finished pair performs. Single vision, progressive and reading lenses are available.

frame-fitting.title: Frame Fitting
frame-fitting.summary: Bridge, temple length and pantoscopic tilt set to your face.
frame-fitting.detail: A frame that fits sits level, rests on the bridge rather than the cheeks, and stays put when you look down. We measure, fit and adjust before you leave with them.

lens-consultation.title: Lens Consultation
lens-consultation.summary: Straight talk about lens material, thickness and coatings.
lens-consultation.detail: We explain the practical differences between lens indexes, anti-reflective and hard coatings, and tinted or photochromic options — then recommend what actually suits your prescription and your day, without upselling.

frame-adjustment.title: Frame Adjustment
frame-adjustment.summary: Free realignment for frames bought with us, any time.
frame-adjustment.detail: Glasses loosen, temples splay, nose pads shift. Bring them in and we will bring them back to true. There is no charge and no appointment needed for frames purchased at KOJIKANE.

eyewear-styling.title: Eyewear Styling
eyewear-styling.summary: An honest second opinion on shape, colour and proportion.
eyewear-styling.detail: We will pull frames you would not have picked up yourself, tell you when something is not working, and narrow six options down to two. Bringing someone whose taste you trust is encouraged.

after-sales-service.title: After-Sales Service
after-sales-service.summary: Nose pads, screws, cleaning and repairs after you buy.
after-sales-service.detail: Small parts wear out long before a good frame does. We replace nose pads and screws, clean frames ultrasonically, and advise on repair when something breaks.

faqs.question: Do I need an appointment?
faqs.answer: No. KOJIKANE EYEWEAR is a walk-in shop. If you would like a longer styling or lens consultation, call ahead on 080-519-6633 and we will keep time free for you.

faqs.question: Can I bring my own prescription?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we encourage it. Bring your most recent prescription from your eye examination and we will work from it when recommending frames and lenses.

faqs.question: Can you put prescription lenses into a fashion frame?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. It depends on the shape and depth of the frame and on your prescription. Bring the frame to the shop and we will tell you honestly whether it will work well.

faqs.question: Do you adjust glasses bought elsewhere?
faqs.answer: We are happy to look at them. Adjustment is free for frames bought at KOJIKANE; for frames from elsewhere, ask us in store and we will tell you what we can do.

faqs.question: How long does a new pair take?
faqs.answer: It depends on the lenses. Simple single-vision pairs are usually quick; specialist lenses and coatings take longer. We will give you a realistic date when you order.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: A short, plain-language summary of what we do with personal information. This page should be reviewed by the shop before launch.

sections.heading: What this website collects
sections.body: This website does not have accounts, a shopping basket, or a contact form. It does not ask you for personal information, and it does not set advertising cookies. It stores one small cookie only if you choose a language, so the site remembers your choice. If analytics are added later, this page will be updated to say which service is used and what it records.

sections.heading: Information you send us directly
sections.body: If you contact us by phone, LINE or Facebook, we see whatever you choose to share — typically your name, your message and, if you send one, a photograph of your prescription. We use it only to answer you and to prepare your order.

sections.heading: Information kept in the shop
sections.body: When you buy glasses from us we keep the record needed to make and service them, including your prescription and the frame details. This is kept so that we can remake or adjust your glasses later. We do not sell it or share it for marketing.

sections.heading: Third-party services
sections.body: Pages on this site may embed a Google Maps view so you can find the shop. Links to LINE and Facebook take you to those services, which have their own privacy policies.

sections.heading: Your choices
sections.body: You can ask us what we hold about you, ask for it to be corrected, or ask us to delete it. Call the shop or send us a message and we will deal with it.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: The short version: this is an information website for a physical shop, and nothing here is a purchase or a medical opinion.

sections.heading: About this website
sections.body: This site presents KOJIKANE EYEWEAR, a family-owned optical shop in Nonthaburi. It is an information website. Nothing can be bought through it, and no order is placed by browsing it.

sections.heading: Frames and availability
sections.body: Frames shown here are photographed for reference. Stock changes, and a particular frame may not be in the shop on the day you visit. Please call or message before travelling if you have your heart set on something specific.

sections.heading: Guidance, not advice
sections.body: Articles in the Journal are general guidance about eyewear and style. They are not eye care advice and are not a substitute for an eye examination by a qualified professional.

sections.heading: Content and images
sections.body: Text and photographs on this site belong to the shop and may not be reproduced without permission. Some images are temporary placeholders and will be replaced with the shop’s own photography.

sections.heading: Links to other sites
sections.body: Links to LINE, Facebook and Google Maps are provided for convenience. We are not responsible for the content of those services.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: These terms may be updated as the site grows. The current version is always the one published here. This page should be reviewed by the shop before launch.
